title: Aldehydes and ketones
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR17a#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR17a#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR17a#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR17a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR17a#N.6, OR17a#N.9, OR17a#N.11, OR17a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ketone
items.clue: Has C=O inside the chain rather than at its end, as in propanone.

items.label: Aldehyde
items.clue: Has C=O at the end of the chain with an H on it; the name ends in -al.

items.label: Hydroxynitrile
items.clue: Product of adding HCN across C=O, e.g. CH₃CH(OH)CN; the chain gains one carbon.

items.label: Carbonyl
items.clue: The C=O group, around which the arrangement is trigonal planar with angles of about 120°.

questions.stem: Butanone, CH₃COCH₂CH₃, is reduced. Reagent: LiAlH₄ in dry ether, then dilute acid. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: CH₃COCH₂CH₃ + 2[H] → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃. A ketone gives a secondary alcohol.

questions.stem: In the mechanism for the reaction of propanone with cyanide, where does the first curly arrow start and end?

options.text: From the lone pair on the N of CN⁻ to the carbonyl carbon
From the lone pair on the C of CN⁻ to the carbonyl carbon
From the C=O π bond to the C of CN⁻
From a lone pair on the carbonyl O to H⁺

questions.explanation: The cyanide carbon's lone pair forms the new C–C bond to the δ+ carbonyl carbon.

questions.stem: Which carbonyl compound gives a racemic mixture when it reacts with HCN?
questions.explanation: The product carbon has CH₃, C₂H₅, OH and CN: a chiral centre. Attack from either face is equally likely, giving a racemate.

questions.stem: Hex-5-en-2-one, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂COCH₃, has a C=C bond and a C=O bond. It is treated with LiAlH₄ in dry ether, then dilute acid. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: H⁻ is a nucleophile. It attacks the δ+ carbon of C=O. The non-polar, electron-rich C=C does not attract it.
